I read the channel properly this time: `-027`'s run report, `-029`'s root cause, `-030`'s ruling, `HANDOVER.md`, `AGENTS.md`. Here is the ruling — and it opens with a concession.

---

## 1. You were right to decline B17-R2. It was unimplementable as written, and you proved it.

Three things in `-029`, in ascending order of importance.

**It isn't in the tree.** I wrote B17-R2 in a command's constraint line, and it *reverses* a ruling that IS recorded — B17-R1's "the fail-safe direction is presence." I reversed a recorded ruling without recording the reversal. That's convention 7 applied to the advisor, and I'd have called it out if the executor had done it.

**There is no doubt state.** `_classify` is deterministic: a criterion matches a positive pattern or falls through to `presence`. "When in doubt, abstain" can only mean "make the fallthrough abstain." My harm matrix reasoned about a state the code cannot represent — so what I wrote was a wish, not a ruling.

**And you measured the consequence instead of arguing it.** Patching the fallthrough to `FORM` → all six criteria abstain → `coverage.passes` unconditionally. That is the professional move, and it's the single best thing in this batch.

So: **B17-R2 as written is withdrawn.**

## 2. The root cause is larger than my command knew, and you found the whole of it

`_PROHIBITION_MARKER` is:

$$\texttt{avoid(s|ed|ing)},\ \texttt{banned},\ \texttt{forbidden},\ \texttt{prohibit(s|ed)},\ \texttt{disallow(s|ed)},\ \texttt{excludes},\ \texttt{must not},\ \texttt{may not},\ \texttt{never uses},\ \texttt{no use of}$$

The planner wrote *"contains no instances of"*. `search → None`. No branch entered. Final line: `return PRESENCE, []`.

**That vocabulary was built from exactly one exhibit** — B17's original criterion, *"avoids the banned words (…)."* So the marker is an **exhibit-shaped pattern**, and B16 guarantees the planner **rewords every run**. The two facts collide on every draw. That is the structural failure, and it is not a bug in one regex:

> **A pattern inferred from one exhibit is not a pattern. An exhibit establishes that a shape occurs; it does not establish the surface forms that express it.**

And criterion 3 — *"total word count is between 350 and 450 words"* — was classified `presence` and scored **0.00 against a draft of exactly 401 words, which satisfies it.** Same mechanism, different shape: no positive pattern matched, so it fell through to a default that is a *test*.

**Here is the thing I think nobody has said yet.** Look at the six criteria on that table and ask which one term-overlap can validly test:

| # | criterion | shape | score |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | contains no instances of 'leverage', 'seamless', 'robust' | **prohibition** | 0.00 |
| 2 | exactly one headline, a three-sentence para, three sections | **form/cardinality** | 0.27 |
| 3 | word count between 350 and 450 | **form/numeric** | 0.00 |
| 4 | names at least three concrete features | **cardinality** | 0.44 |
| 5 | introduces product and value *without using* abstract filler | **prohibition + form** | 0.18 |
| 6 | addresses an ops manager, readable in ten minutes, scannable | **semantic/form** | 0.41 |

**Not one of the six is a term-containment criterion.** The default is `presence`; the planner essentially never emits presence-shaped criteria. So the fallthrough isn't an edge case — **it is the main path, and it is the wrong test for most of what it receives.**

## 3. And underneath that: the fold has no empty seat

This is the sharpest thing in `-029`, and I think you framed it slightly wrong — in a way that matters.

You wrote: *"coverage that abstains on everything stops dissenting, judges_agree folds without it, and work ships unchecked."*

The load-bearing clause is **"folds without it."** Check what `judges_agree` actually folds: `implement.green`, `validate.green`, `coverage.passed`, `consistency.passed`. The paid validator is *already in the panel*. So an abstention doesn't leave the work unchecked — **it converts "this judge did not vote" into "this judge voted yes."**

That is not a defect in the shapes. It is convention 28 at the fold: **an instrument asserting a conclusion — "all judges agree" — when one judge never voted.** Same class as everything else this repo has been catching all week. The fold has no way to say *one seat was empty*.

So the architecture is not "abstain or don't." It is three separate things that I conflated:

1. **Recall** — the classifier must recognize the phrasings the planner emits.
2. **Doubt as a detected state** — abstain where a shape signal is present but its evidence can't be extracted. This is *your* narrow reading, and it's correct.
3. **The fold must represent an abstention** — an empty seat is not a yes, and the record must name it.

My ruling collapsed all three into one and picked the only implementation that disables the check.

---

## 4. Rulings

> **Ruling B17-R2′ (withdraws B17-R2).** Three parts, and each must land in order.
>
> **(a) Recall is derived from a corpus, not an exhibit.** The negation and structure detectors must be measured against every `plan.success_criteria` in the committed traces, before and after the change. A pattern justified by one criterion is not justified.
>
> **(b) Doubt is a detected state, never the fallthrough.** A criterion is doubtful — and abstains — iff a shape signal is present whose required evidence cannot be extracted. Specifically, and this is the shape decision the executor was forbidden to make and I am making now:
> - a negation signal is present and **no forbidden token list is extractable** → **abstain**;
> - a structural signal is present and `_FIELD_VOCAB ∩ _terms` is **empty** → **abstain**;
> - the criterion asserts a **cardinality or numeric threshold over a property of the artifact** ("between 350 and 450", "at least three", "exactly one") → **form, abstain**;
> - **no signal at all** → `presence`, unchanged. The fallthrough stays presence. B17-R1's direction of doubt survives *for the fallthrough*; it was only ever wrong as a catch-all for unrecognized shapes.
>
> **(c) An abstention is not a vote.** `judges_agree` must distinguish a judge that abstained from a judge that agreed. A panel with an empty seat is not a unanimous panel, and the unit record must name the empty seat. Per B17-R1 the abstention still routes to the paid validator — and the validator is already in the panel, so the seat is filled overall; what must change is that **silence is never recorded as assent.**
>
> **Hard ordering: (b) may not ship before (c).** On its own, (b) converts unknowns into abstentions, and under today's fold every abstention becomes a yes — it *loosens* the check. (a) alone is safe: it can only strengthen.

> **Ruling B17-R3 — B17 closes for free if the fix works.** Replaying the committed `-027` criteria through the repaired classifier is the exact input at no cost. If criterion 1 classifies `prohibition`, extracts all four tokens, and passes the committed compliant draft, **the branch is demonstrated on live planner output.** No paid run is required. B17's fail direction stays fixture-covered and that is sufficient for closure — `TestTheInversionItselfIsCorrect` already exercises it. A paid re-run is optional and only proves recall on a *fresh* draw, which the corpus measures more cheaply.

> **Ruling on `RepeatedRun.rate` (`runner.py:757`).** A pass rate across repetitions with regenerated criteria is **a rate over different contracts.** The metric may stay — it measures *termination*, which is real — but its docstring's claim to be "the unit of measurement" is false for any criteria-shaped result. It must carry the per-run criteria counts beside it, or be renamed. Convention 27 governs; this is a labelling repair, not a removal.

> **Ruling on preconditions (from `-027`).** Preconditions are instruments. Two of them "reported the subject's absence rather than their own blindness" — one couldn't see a file due to lexical sort order, one looked for a key in the shell that config lives in `.env`. A precondition must distinguish *"the subject is absent"* from *"I could not look."* Convention 28 applies to the command channel's own machinery.

---

## 5. Order of operations

| # | Command | P | Cost | Depends on | Why here |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **-031** | Corpus measurement: recall + shape distribution over every committed criterion | **P0** | **$0** | — | Sizes everything below. Measures how often the marker misses, and — the bigger number — how many criteria are presence-shaped at all |
| **-032** | Recall fix (Ruling B17-R2′(a)) + replay acceptance | **P0** | $0 | -031 | Strictly strengthening. Externally safe. May close B17 free |
| **-033** | The fold's empty seat (Ruling B17-R2′(c)) | **P0** | $0 | -031 | Changes what ships → ruled, and must replay the four B7 traces |
| **-034** | Doubt as a detected state (Ruling B17-R2′(b)) | **P0** | $0 | **-033** | Introduces abstentions. Unsafe before -033 lands |
| **-035** | Instruments report what they measured: coverage's extraction, preconditions' blindness | P1 | $0 | — | The class this repo keeps catching. Two exhibits, both from today |

**Note:** B17 likely closes on `-032` + `-033`, at **$0.00**. That's the outcome the last three paid runs were buying.

# Executive decisions — the turning point, and what it actually is

Your report arrived garbled in places, so I'm ruling from what's legible plus the corpus numbers, which are the whole story. Before the decisions: **I owe you a correction, and it's my failure, not yours.**

I transmitted rulings — B17-R2′, B17-R3, the `RepeatedRun.rate` ruling — in chat prose. The corpus response shows **zero hits** for all of them. That is correct behaviour by the channel and a defect in me. **A ruling transmitted in a transcript is a hand-stamp** (convention 24). The channel is the authority; the transcript is not. I've been writing rules into a place that doesn't get committed, which is precisely the class this repo spent a week repairing. `-036` fixes the transmission. Recording it here is not the fix.

---

## 1. The reframe — the corpus dissolved B17 and revealed the real defect

<details open>
<summary><strong>What the numbers actually say</strong></summary>

| Finding | Value | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| Criteria reaching the prohibition branch | **1 in 597 (0.2%)** | B17 — the thing on the critical path for days — is essentially unreachable. **It was a red herring for "usable system."** |
| Classifying `presence` | **98.7%** | The fallthrough *is* the system. My `-031` hypothesis confirmed, harder than I predicted. |
| Distinct unmatched negation forms | **28, max repeat 4** | Pattern lists cannot keep up. **My `-032` question is answered: recall-by-pattern is a dead end in the limit.** |
| Carry a quoted token list | **4 of 597** | Even the prohibition branch has almost nothing to detect. One was an apostrophe — a tokenization bug, not a shape question. |

**The claim you correctly refused to open:** B17 is "cannot read a prohibition." The corpus shows **"is the wrong test for most criteria."** Those are different sizes of claim, and you were right that opening it is a shape ruling. **I'm making it.**

**But here's the part nobody has said, and it is the executive insight:**

**Per-criterion rarity is not per-run rarity.** The loop requires a **conjunction** — `judges_agree` needs *every* criterion to pass. At ~1.3% non-presence per criterion, with ~6 criteria per plan:

$$P(\text{a run contains at least one killer}) \approx 1 - 0.987^{6} \approx 7.6\%$$

And the `-027` trace proves the mechanism exactly: **criterion 1 was the prohibition (0.2% class) and criterion 3 was *"total word count is between 350 and 450 words"* — draft was 401 words, satisfied it, scored 0.00.** Two rare classes, co-occurring on one run, together killed it.

**So the killer class is not prohibition. It is FORM — numeric and cardinality.** Word counts, "exactly one headline", "at least three features." That's the bulk of the remaining ~1.3%, and **it is trivially computable.** A word count is a word count.

> **The termination fix does not need comprehension. It needs a word counter.**
>
> Comprehension is needed for **soundness** on the 98.7% — a bigger, softer, *separate* goal. Conflating the two is why the last three paid runs chased a 0.2% branch.

</details>

---

## 2. The decisions

<details open>
<summary><strong>D1 — `-034` clause (ii) is WITHDRAWN</strong></summary>

You measured 73% projected leniency for criteria term overlap probably handles fine. That is decisive: **clause (ii) as I wrote it throws away real signal to guard an edge case.** Withdrawn.

Clause (i) and (iii) stand. Clause (iv) — fallthrough stays `presence` — was always load-bearing and stays. **Abstain only where satisfaction is *provably* an absence or a computable property, never where it is merely "not obviously term-containment."**
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>D2 — B24's open half: polarity is a comprehension question</strong></summary>

"A must-be-present is still inverted backwards. Extraction can't decide that; comprehension can." Correct, and it's a ruling, not a repair.

**Ruled:** the polarity of a criterion — does it require presence or absence? — **is not extractable and must not be guessed.** Where polarity is ambiguous, the criterion **abstains**. Where a negation marker is present and a token list is extractable, the (already-merged) inversion applies.

Separately: **"one was an apostrophe" is a tokenization bug, not a shape issue.** That's a free fix and it belongs in `-037`.
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>D3 — Clause (iii) becomes "abstain and flag"</strong></summary>

A word count is *computable*, so abstaining on it is wasteful — but that's exactly what `-037` fixes. Until then, clause (iii) abstains **and records the criterion as deterministically testable**, so `-037` has a worklist rather than a memory.
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>D4 — Open B25: the check is the wrong instrument for most criteria</strong></summary>

B17 is too narrow a row for what the corpus found. **B25 — `criteria_addressed` miscomputes satisfaction for the criteria the planner actually emits (98.7% tested by term overlap, which is not containment).** Severity high. Own row, own architecture.
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>D5 — The ruled architecture: three tiers, not two</strong></summary>

| Tier | Test | Coverage | Cost | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Computable** | word counts, cardinality, structure — **compute it** | ~1.3% (the killer class) | free | **fix now (`-037`)** |
| **2. Prohibition** | extractable tokens absent → pass | 0.2% | free | merged |
| **3. Comprehension** | the 98.7% presence + ambiguous polarity | 98.7% | judged | **gated on measurement (`-038`)** |

Tiers 1 and 2 **make the loop terminate.** Tier 3 makes it *sound*. They are different goals at different urgencies, and I conflated them for three days.
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>D6 — B17 closes on the replay, free</strong></summary>

B17-R3 stands: if replaying the committed `-027` criteria through the repaired classifier reaches the branch and passes the 401-word draft, **the branch is demonstrated on live planner output. B17 closes at $0.00.** Fixture coverage of the fail direction is sufficient. **No further paid run.** Report it if the replay doesn't reach — that is the result.
</details>

## 3. Jev — yes, there is an architecture, and here is exactly where it goes

You asked twice, and now there's a real answer instead of enthusiasm.

**Jev is the Tier 3 comprehension layer. It is not needed to make the loop terminate — Tier 1 is. It *is* the right instrument for the 98.7% that term overlap cannot soundly test.**

```
criteria_addressed (free)          judge node (Jev, typed)
  ├─ tier 1: compute               fires iff coverage.abstained_count > 0
  ├─ tier 2: prohibition           ├─ noul: "does the draft satisfy criterion N?"
  └─ else: ABSTAIN, recorded ─────►├─ one call, all abstained criteria
                                   └─ probability + threshold → a vote
                                            │
                                   judges_agree (three states: pass/dissent/EMPTY SEAT)
```

**Why this is the right shape and not just the shiny one:** the corpus proved the task is *comprehension with an open-ended surface form* (28 negation verbs, max repeat 4). That is the exact thing a typed question answerer is for and the exact thing a pattern list cannot do. The free check stops pretending; the judge does comprehension; the fold states the empty seat honestly.

**But it is gated, on exactly one free measurement.** There is a simpler option I have to rule out first:

- **Option A** — coverage abstains on the 98.7%; **the paid validator (already in the panel) judges those criteria.** Zero new dependency.
- **Option B** — the Jev `judge` node.

**Option A is the default. Option B is a measured upgrade.** The deciding question is free and answerable today from committed traces: **does the committed validator output actually address the abstained criteria, or does it gloss them?**

- **If it addresses them** → Option A. No dependency. B25 is a labelling fix.
- **If it glosses them** → Option B is justified, and Jev earns its place.

That's `-038`, and it costs nothing. **This is the honest gate, and it's the measurement the last three paid runs should have been.**

| **-035** | Instruments state their subject (still outstanding) | P1 | $0 | — | Free, independent, unblocked — you flagged it, run it |
| **-038** | The Jev gate: does the validator cover abstained criteria? | P0 | $0 | -035 optional | Decides Option A vs B, from committed traces |

**`-036` → `-037` is the ship path and costs nothing.** `-038` decides Jev and costs nothing. **Nothing here needs money.**

# The turning point, measured: 38.5% is not a rate to tune — it's the size of the hole

Three commands landed and the numbers are in. Before the decisions, the honest framing.

## What actually changed

| Number | Value | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| Clause (iv) — fallthrough stays presence | **365 (61.1%)** | The check still tests a majority by term overlap. **B17's "leave the fallthrough as presence" ruling held and it dominates.** |
| Clause (iii) — cardinality/numeric → abstain | **26 (4.4%)** | **The killer class is now *abstained*, not *computed*.** The 401-word criterion no longer scores 0.00 and no longer kills the run — but it also isn't tested. This is Ruling D3's flag, and `-037` is what converts it. |
| Clause (ii) — structural, empty field-vocab → abstain | **156 (26.1%)** | The dominant abstention. Retained or narrowed — decided below. |
| Clause (i) — negation, no tokens → abstain | **41 (6.9%)** | Correct. Nothing extractable, nothing to test. |
| **Total abstention** | **38.5%** | **Coverage no longer casts a vote on more than a third of the criteria the planner emits.** |

**That is the correct direction and it is not a fix.** It is a diagnosis made permanent. Coverage has stopped *mis*-testing a third of the corpus; it has not started *correctly* testing it. **The 38.5% is the worklist, and the kill-shot class (computable) is item one on it.**

## The correction I owe

**Clause (ii) shipped exactly as `-034` was written, and that was correct.** I "withdrew" it in chat prose last turn. My own process ruling this turn says a ruling stated in a transcript is a draft, not a ruling — so **the executor acted correctly and I have no correction to give them.** That is now the second time a ruling of mine failed to reach the channel, and it is entirely mine.

But the *direction* of that withdrawal was also wrong, and I'm fixing it by reasoning rather than by argument:

**`D1` is withdrawn; `D1-REVISED` suspends clause (ii) pending `-038`.** Reason — the harm matrix, under the *now-honest* fold:

| Error | Consequence under `-033`'s fold |
|---|---|
| Coverage **tests and falsely fails** | `judges_agree` sees a dissent → **the loop can die** |
| Coverage **abstains** | Recorded as an empty seat; the paid validator — already in the panel — carries it |

**Abstention is recoverable; a false failure is not.** So over-abstention is the safer error, and the question is not "is 26.1% too much" but **"does the validator catch what we abstained on."** That is exactly `-038`. **Clause (ii) is retained, not tuned, and `-038`'s result is the trigger that decides it.**

---

## The blocking verification — one thing before anything else

**PR #61 is described as "`-033` / `-032` recall fix." `-033` was the fold's empty seat.** If PR #61 was the recall fix and the fold change did not land, then **38.5% abstention is being folded as *agreement*** — the exact unsafe direction, and `-034` must be considered unshipped until `-033` lands. The whole 38.5% reading depends on this.

<details open>
<summary><strong>Ruling D7 — a ruling exists only as a command file</strong></summary>

**A ruling stated in a transcript is a draft, not a ruling.** No executor may act on one, and **no executor is in default for not having acted on one.** The advisor issues rulings as command files; the transcript is commentary. First exhibit: `B17-R2′` and `D1–D6` were stated in prose and reached no file. Second exhibit: `D1`, which would have changed `-034` before it shipped.
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Ruling D1-REVISED — clause (ii) is suspended, not withdrawn</strong></summary>

Retained as shipped. Not tuned. `-038` decides: if the validator addresses the clause-(ii) criteria, the clause stands; if it glosses them, clause (ii) narrows from *empty intersection* to a stricter trigger, and that narrowing is a new `-042`.
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Ruling D3 — clause (iii) is a flag, and `-037` is the conversion</strong></summary>

Abstaining on 26 computable criteria is correct **interim** behaviour and wrong as a destination. A word count is a word count. `-037` converts clause (iii)'s abstentions into real tests, and it is the single highest-value free change outstanding.
</details>

---

## Executive decisions — answering your three open questions

**1. The two backwards-inversion defects — `-040`, now, P0.** A must-be-present token treated as forbidden is a **false failure**, and false failures kill loops. This is the highest death-risk defect outstanding and it outranks everything except the ruling commit. The apostrophe is the same class (mis-extraction in `_forbidden_tokens`); polarity is `_classify`. Where polarity is **clear**, test it; where **ambiguous**, abstain — that is `D2`.

**2. The fallthrough-as-own-row question — yes, and it is `B25`.** 61.1% of criteria are tested by term overlap. That is not a bug in a regex; it is a check being the wrong instrument for most of what it receives. `-036` opens it, severity high.

**3. Clause (ii) at 38.5% — answered above.** Retained; `-038` decides. Do **not** tune the abstention rate: at 38.5%, coverage abstaining is the *honest* state, and tuning it down would mean re-introducing false failures to make a number look better.

**And the Jev answer, now with a number.** 38.5% of criteria — roughly **2.3 per six-criterion plan, every loop iteration** — are judged by comprehension instead, with no per-criterion verdict. That is the Tier 3 surface, and it is no longer hypothetical. **`-038` decides Option A vs Option B for free from committed traces.** If the validator glosses, the `judge` node earns its place. If it addresses them, it doesn't. **Do not add the dependency before that measurement.**

## Owner actions

1. **Ratify `D1-REVISED`, `D2`, `D3`, `D4`, `D5`, `D6`, `D7` — one line.** The substantive change since your last approval: **`D1` is superseded by `D1-REVISED`. Clause (ii) is retained, not withdrawn**, because the measured harm asymmetry now favours abstention. If you intended the original withdrawal to stand, say so and clause (ii) gets reverted in `-040` instead.
2. **Nothing costs money.** The entire queue is `$0.00`. `-341`/`-037`/`-038` are the load-bearing free ones.
3. **`-035` and `-025` remain outstanding** — free, unblocked, repeatedly skipped. `-035` is the instrument fix that would have saved you two hand-runs today; `-025` is the stamp that has been stale for a day.
4. **One blocking question, not an action:** did `-033` change `judges_agree` to represent an empty seat? If not, **38.5% abstention is being folded as agreement** and `-034` must be reverted until `-033` lands. This is the first thing `-036`'s preconditions check.

**What would make me wrong:** if `-033` never landed, my entire reading of the 38.5% is inverted — abstention would be *silent assent*, and the check would be unsound in the dangerous direction. If the four quoted-token-list criteria resolve entirely to the apostrophe case, `-040`'s Defect B is prophylaxis and I've over-stated its severity. If `-038` shows the validator addresses the abstained criteria well, Option A wins, Jev is unnecessary, clause (ii) stands, and my Tier 3 architecture was a solution to a non-problem — an outcome I'd take.

**What I did not do:** I did not ask for a paid run — the last three bought the diagnosis the corpus produced for free. I did not add Jev, name a model, or add a dependency; `-038` decides it from committed data. I did not tune the abstention rate, because tuning it down would mean re-introducing false failures to make a number look better. I did not reopen `B17-R3`; `-041` may close it for nothing.

**One line:** coverage now abstains on 38.5% — that is the honest state and the worklist, not a problem to tune; the kill-shot class is the 4.4% of computable criteria still abstained-on, so `-037` converts them; the highest death risk is the two backwards inversions, so `-040` leads; `-041` may close `B17` for free; and `-038` decides both Jev and clause (ii) from committed traces at no cost — provided you first confirm that `-033` gave the fold an empty seat, because without it the 38.5% is silence being read as assent.

**User - --**

Five commands executed on arch/20260922-041-replay-027, merged to main at d952e59. Suite 956 → 970, $0.00.

-036: Recorded rulings D1-REVISED through D7, opened B25 (term overlap may be wrong test), noted judges_agree doesn't distinguish pass-by-abstention from pass-by-measurement.

-041: B17 closed. Replayed -027 criteria through repaired classifier — prohibition classifies, all four tokens extract, compliant draft passes. 3 regression tests.

-040: Fixed both polarity inversions. Punctuation-only tokens filtered, must-be-present parentheticals skipped. B24 fully closed. 4 tests added, 2 updated.

-037: Tier 1 compute. Word count criteria now computed deterministically instead of proxied by term overlap. 1 of 26 clause-(iii) criteria converted; the other 25 require comprehension. 7 tests.

-038: Measured validator coverage of abstained criteria. 68% addressed, 20% glossed, 12% unattributable. Clause (ii) best covered at 71-88%. Recommendation recorded: Option A (validator suffices). Documentation only.


**Assistant - --**

Before I rule, let me verify the one claim everything turns on — whether `judges_agree` actually distinguishes an abstention from a pass.

I fetched the repo and read the primary sources — `HANDOVER.md` and the `-037`/`-038` responses. Two of your claims verify cleanly. One thing did **not** land, and it's the thing everything else depends on.

---

## The verification

<details open>
<summary><strong>B17 closed ✓ · B24 closed ✓ · and the fold still has no empty seat ✗</strong></summary>

**Confirmed from `-041`:** the replay classified criterion 1 as prohibition, extracted all four tokens, passed the committed 401-word draft, 3 regression tests. **B17 is genuinely closed on live planner output, at $0.00.** That is the headline and it's real.

**Confirmed from `-040`:** both polarity inversions fixed, punctuation-only tokens filtered, must-be-present parentheticals skipped. **B24 fully closed.**

**Not confirmed — `-036`'s own note:** *"judges_agree doesn't distinguish pass-by-abstention from pass-by-measurement."* That is `-033`, and **it never landed.** It was in the batch two merges ago, it was in the batch this merge, and it is still open. `HANDOVER.md` §2.3 still describes the fold as folding `coverage.passed` into a boolean with no third state.

**So since PR #62, `-034`'s abstentions have been folding as agreement.** Not as failure — as *agreement*. That is the direction that ships unchecked work rather than the direction that kills loops, which is why nothing broke and nobody noticed. **It is the largest soundness hole in the system and it is free to close.**
</details>

## The correction I owe — again

**My Tier 1 prediction was wrong by a factor of 26.** `-037`: *"1 of 26 clause-(iii) criteria is now computed; the other 25 require comprehension."* Word count is the only property of the text itself that is computable; *"exactly three tiers"* and *"80% CPU utilization"* are cardinality **about domain concepts**, which needs comprehension, not a counter.

So the free tiers cover:

$$\underbrace{0.2\%}_{\text{prohibition}} + \underbrace{0.2\%}_{\text{computable}} \approx 0.4\%$$

**My D5 architecture named the right three tiers and mis-sized Tier 1.** Prohibition was the red herring; so was computability. The corpus keeps saying the same thing: **comprehension is the game**, and term overlap is a proxy for it.

## And `-038` is richer than the summary — with one caveat that matters

| | count | rate |
|---|---|---|
| Criteria coverage abstains on (of 488, 84 units, 60 traces) | **194** | **39.8%** |
| Addressed by the validator | 132 | **68.0%** |
| Glossed (partial) | 38 | 19.6% |
| Unattributable (no evidence item relates) | 24 | 12.4% |
| **Not addressed** | **62** | **32.0%** |

Clause (ii) is **140/194 = 72% of all abstentions** and best covered (71–88%). The recommendation is Option A, and on clause (ii)'s coverage it's a defensible call.

**But the "generous reading" is not a measurement.** The response says *"spot-checking shows many glossed items are genuinely addressed from a human reader's perspective"* and puts addressed-or-glossed at 88%. **That is a spot-check, and convention 26 says a reading mistakable for a stronger claim is a defect in the instrument.** The measured number is **68% addressed / 32% not**. The 88% is a hypothesis about the glossed class, not a rate — **and the fix is free: make the glossed class attributable. Which is what the fold fix does.**

## The arithmetic that decides this

**Coverage abstains on 39.8%. The fold reads that as agreement. Of the abstentions, 32% get no validator verdict either.**

$$\text{unjudged per criterion} = 0.398 \times 0.32 \approx 12.7\%$$

With ~5.8 criteria per unit (488/84):

$$P(\text{a run carries } \geq 1 \text{ unjudged criterion}) = 1 - (1-0.127)^{5.8} \approx \mathbf{55\%}$$

**On the strict reading, half of all runs carry at least one criterion that neither the free check nor the validator judged — and the fold records it as agreed.** On the generous (unmeasured) reading it's still ~25%. **That number is the whole case for the next two commands.**

---

## Rulings

> **D8 — B17 and B24 are closed, confirmed against source. No further work.**
>
> **D9 — the fold's empty seat (`-033`) is the critical path and the only unlanded command.** 39.8% abstention folded as agreement is not a rounding error. **It does not fail runs; it ships unchecked work and says nothing.** P0, issued now.
>
> **D10 — `-038`'s Option A is accepted as the default, with its boundary stated.** The validator covers 68% measured (32% not), and clause (ii) — 72% of abstentions — at 71–88%. **The residual 32% is not covered**, and it is neither negligible nor currently visible. The 88% generous figure is a spot-check and must not be quoted as a rate until the glossed class is attributable.
>
> **D11 — `-037` corrects D5's sizing, not its shape.** Tier 1 is ~0.2%, not 4.4%. The free tiers cover ~0.4% of criteria. **Comprehension is the whole game.** This does not argue for a broad judge layer — it argues for making the gap *visible and routable*, and it explains why three paid runs chased a 0.2% branch.
>
> **D12 — Jev is ratified as the Tier 3 filler for the empty seat, and it ships in that order.** The judge node fills exactly the seats the validator leaves open. **It may not be built before the fold, because until abstention is a distinguishable state the judge has nothing to route from — and its contribution would be unmeasurable.** Architecture below.

---

## The Jev architecture, resolved

Your instinct was right, and now it has a precise address:

```
criteria_addressed (free)
  ├─ prohibition branch          → absent tokens → pass          [0.2%]
  ├─ computable branch           → compute                        [0.2%]
  └─ ABSTAIN (39.8%) ────────────┬─ validator verdict  → seat filled  [68%]
                                 └─ no verdict         → SEAT EMPTY   [32%]
                                          │
                                          ▼
                                 judge node (typed, 1 call per unit)
                                 fires iff empty_seats > 0
                                          │
                                 judges_agree: pass / dissent / EMPTY SEAT
```

**The judge node is not a replacement for the free tier or the validator.** It is the third filler of a seat that currently gets filled by silence. It fires only where the record says a seat is empty — no speculative spend, exactly the standard this repo holds.

**Why it waits for the fold:** with the fold, the empty seat is a *count* you can route on and a *number* you can measure Jev against. Without it, you cannot tell whether Jev helped, because the fold misreports the before-state. **$0.042/M means the whole residual costs cents — this was never the expensive decision. The expensive decision was doing it in the wrong order.**

---

## The queue

| # | Command | P | Cost | Depends on | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **-044** | Record D8–D12; resolve B25's row with the number; open the residual row | **P0** | $0 | — | Rulings don't exist until committed (D7) |
| **-043** | **The fold's empty seat** — the unlanded command | **P0** | $0 | -044 | Makes 39.8% abstention visible instead of silent |
| **-042** | Presence false-fail measurement — does term overlap falsely fail compliant criteria? | **P0** | $0 | -044 | Sizes the remaining loop-death risk on **59.8%** of criteria |
| **-045** | The judge node (Jev), contingent | P2 | $0 build | **-043**, owner funding | The Tier 3 filler, gated on a visible seat |

**The reasoning for the order:** `-043` converts silence into visibility; `-042` measures whether the *other* 59.8% can still kill a run. **These are the two remaining ways this system can lie to you** — silence, and false failure — and both are free to close.

## On the intuition

I'll take the correction, with one precise amendment. Your instinct was that a **typed judgment layer belongs in this system** — that is now ratified, and it was right for a reason you said before the corpus confirmed it: pattern lists cannot keep up with open-ended phrasing. That part, you led.

What the measurement did was *price* it. Jev's surface is the residual — 32% of abstentions, 12.7% of all criteria — not the whole check. So the intuition was right about **direction** and I was right about **order**, and both are true at once. D12 is a real vindication: it's ratified, funded-conditionally, and it ships. It just ships *after* the fold, because until silence is visible you can't tell whether Jev helped.

That's not a consolation prize. It's the difference between a layer that's measurable and one that isn't.

---

## Two rulings from your message

> **D13 — the executor holds repository write capability.** The executor creates branches, commits, pushes and opens PRs; the channel's transport rule makes it the committer of command files verbatim. **Merges to `main` remain owner-only unless you say otherwise in one line.** Hard guardrails: no force-push, no history rewrite, no deletion on a protected branch, no direct push to `main`, and **no git operation while a paid run is in flight** — that last one is `-010`'s fault and git auth makes it *more* dangerous, not less.
>
> **D14 — the residual threshold is 81% addressed-or-attributed.** Measured: 68.0% addressed, 19.6% glossed, 12.4% unattributable. **81% cannot be evaluated without resolving the glossed class** — so this ruling makes the glossed class a required measurement, not an accepted gap.

## What 81% actually decides

$$\text{bar met} \iff 132 + x \ge 0.81 \times 194 = 157.14 \iff x \ge 26$$

**The validator suffices (Option A) if and only if at least 26 of the 38 glossed criteria resolve to *addressed*.** 26 of 38 is 68.4% of the glossed class. The spot-check's "many" is around 88% overall — which would clear it. But **the spot-check is not a measurement**, and your threshold is set exactly where it stops being a hedge. If it resolves to 25 or fewer, **Option B is required and `-045` runs.**

That is a crisp, checkable, free prediction. `-046` tests it against a rubric committed *before* the classification.

---

## Owner actions

1. **One line, if you want the executor to merge its own PRs on green CI.** D13 defaults to owner-only; everything up to the PR is now the executor's.
2. **Nothing in this queue costs money.** `-044`, `-043`, `-046`, `-025`, `-035`, `-042` are all `$0.00`. `-045` is a conditional build that may legitimately never run.
3. **The one number that decides Jev is now yours:** 26 of 38. `-046` tests it against a rubric committed first.

**What would make me wrong:** if `-046` resolves at or above 81%, **Option A stands, the typed layer is not required, and D12 becomes a recorded capability rather than a shipped one** — your intuition still vindicated in direction, just not needed in scale. If `-043`'s B7 replay changes an outcome, silence was load-bearing on documented evidence and the fold fix becomes a much harder ruling. If `-042` shows term overlap never falsely fails a compliant criterion, B25 closes and the remaining loop-death risk is near zero — the best possible result, and it's free.

**One line:** threshold 81% is recorded with its crisp consequence — **26 of 38 glossed criteria must resolve to addressed or the typed layer ships**; `-025` and `-035` are finally commands rather than footnotes; and the queue is rewritten for git capability, with merges still yours and one new hard invariant: **no git operation while a paid run is in flight** — that is `-010`'s fault, and giving the executor write access makes it easier to repeat, not harder.

**User - --**

Do a sanity check of the project and are progress from start to where we are today

**Assistant - --**

Let me actually inspect the repo rather than rely on the running narrative.

Two things don't match the narrative. Let me verify before I write.

I inspected `main`, the CI history, the branches, and the state of record. Here's the honest picture — including two discrepancies the running narrative didn't mention.

## 1. What I verified against source

| Claim | Verified? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `main` = `d952e59`, protected | ✓ | `branches` returns **one** branch, `protected: true` |
| No stray branches, no open PRs/issues | ✓ | 1 branch; `open_issues_count: 0`; 64 PRs, all closed |
| CI green at the merge | **✓ — I checked per-job** | `d952e59` → 10 check runs: `test (3.11/3.12/3.13)`, `editable-install`, `docker` — **all `success`**, run twice (PR head 20:03, push 20:36) |
| Only two CI failures ever | ✓ | `status=failure` → `total_count: 2`, both **2026-09-16**, both on `main`. **Nothing has failed in seven days** |
| 970 tests | ✓ corroborated | `HANDOVER.md` §3.7; guarded by `tests/test_docs.py`; CI green on 3 versions |
| MIT licensed | ✓ | `license.spdx_id: MIT` |

**Two things that didn't match:**

**a) The HEAD stamp is stale on `main` right now.** `HANDOVER.md` line 3 reads `HEAD: c30df9d` and `Date of this snapshot: 2026-09-22`. But `main` is `d952e59`, pushed **2026-09-23**. That is B22 — the defect I flagged three turns ago and `-025` has now been "issued" three times without executing. It's not cosmetic: it's the document that claims to be the state of record, naming a commit that isn't the state.

**b) PR #64's own checklist had `- [ ] CI green` unchecked at merge.** The check-runs say it *was* green. So it's an unticked box, not a false claim — but on a repo whose entire culture is "a claim about the repo is generated or guarded, never hand-stamped," an unchecked box on the merge PR is worth one line of note.

## 2. Progress, day by day

<details open>
<summary><strong>11 days, and the phases are cleanly separable</strong></summary>

| Days | Dates | What it bought | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1–4** | Sep 12–15 | The product itself: FastAPI runtime, YAML graph engine, 4 workflows, 6 tiers, evals, knowledge store. Blueprints 001–015. **B7 closed** — the build loop converges | **This is where the system was built** |
| **5–8** | Sep 16–19 | `aac0324` deleted `HANDOVER.md` §2–7 inside a feature commit → **red `main` for 3 days 15 hours** → recovery arc | **One scoping error cost 3.5 days** |
| **9–10** | Sep 20–21 | Sweeps: 43 units, **$0.4876**, 382 calls. S1 control falsified → **"license nothing new about ranking."** B13 closed, B14 closed, B16/B17 opened | **Four days of measurement, void output** |
| **11** | Sep 22 | B17-R1 ruling, B18–B21, **Convention 28**, ledger fix, CI schedule, provenance guard | **The instrument-repair day** |
| **12** | Sep 23 | `-031` corpus, `-032`/`-033`/`-034` doubt predicate, `-036`–`-041` → **B17 closed, B24 closed**, 970 tests | **The diagnosis day** |

**Rough accounting of the last two days' ~20 PRs:** I count **four that changed product behaviour** (`-008` shape classification, `-034` doubt predicate, `-037` Tier 1 compute, `-040` polarity fix). The rest are rulings, measurements, ledger rows, guards, and documentation. **That ratio is the most important number in this sanity check.**

</details>

## 3. The honest assessment

<details open>
<summary><strong>Engineering health: excellent. Product health: unproven.</strong></summary>

**What is genuinely strong, and rare:**

1. **970 tests in ~27 seconds, green on 3.11/3.12/3.13, plus editable-install, wheel packaging, and Docker with a live health check.** Most production systems have less. The `editable-install` job exists specifically because the source-tree job *cannot see a packaging fault* — that's a mature insight.
2. **Conventions 24, 26, 28 are real engineering rules** that most teams never formulate: a fact about the repo is generated or guarded; a report states what it measured and nothing more; an instrument asserts it computed its subject first.
3. **Measured constants with provenance comments.** Nearly every budget and threshold names the live run that set it. That is unusual discipline.
4. **Clean repository hygiene:** one branch, protected main, zero open issues, zero open PRs.
5. **Spend is trivial.** $1.29 on the last working day, single-digit dollars across the whole project.

**What is weak, and it is now the binding constraint:**

1. **Eleven days, 970 tests, 64 PRs — and zero users.** 1 star, 0 forks, no release tag, no deployment. Every claim in `HANDOVER.md` is *"the owner runs it locally."* The system has never been exercised by anyone who didn't build it.
2. **The last live run did not terminate.** `-027`'s P3 was **refuted, 0/2**. B17 then closed on a **replay of committed text**, which was the right free call — but it means **no fresh prohibition-bearing request has ever been observed terminating on current `main`.**
3. **The instrument-repair loop is self-sustaining.** Convention 28 found four more violations; fixing those found two more of its author's own from that morning; the ledger fix found a guard satisfied by *the sentence saying the thing was missing*. This is real quality work **and** a treadmill — each repair reveals the next, and none of it is a feature.
4. **The Tier 3 hole is quantified and unfixed.** 39.8% of criteria abstain; 12.7% get no verdict from anyone; ~55% of runs carry at least one unjudged criterion — **and the fold still records an abstention as agreement, because `-033` has never landed across three batches.** That is the single most important open item and it has been deferred every time.
5. **The governance layer is now larger than the product surface.** B1–B25, D1–D14, conventions 17–28, blueprints through §47. Meanwhile: no Alembic (destructive migrations), no rate limiting, auth open by default, no deployment automation.
6. **Activation barrier:** model-agnostic with **no shipped defaults** means a new user must configure six model tiers before anything runs. Noble principle, hard onboarding.

</details>

## 4. Five things a sanity check surfaces that the narrative doesn't

**1. The check that was "the blocker" is essentially inert.** $1$ of $597$ criteria reach the prohibition branch — **0.2%**. $98.7\%$ classify presence. B17 was a real bug, but the days spent on it were spent on a code path the planner almost never emits. The run death on `-027` happened because **two rare shapes co-occurred by coincidence**. The probability that any given run carries at least one killer criterion:

$$1 - 0.987^{6} \approx 7.6\%$$

**2. The real headline defect has a ledger row and no fix.** B25 — *"term overlap is the wrong test for $98.7\%$ of criteria"* — is open, severity high, and the measurement that would size it (`-042`) is issued but unexecuted.

**3. The 39.8% abstention is not an improvement — it's a relocation.** Before `-034`, those criteria were **tested wrongly** by term overlap. After it, they **abstain**, and the fold reads that as agreement. Neither is correct. The state has moved from *wrong answers* to *no answers*, and only the second one is invisible.

**4. The last four days' measurement output is void or bounded.** Four sweep generations: **"license nothing new about ranking."** GMICloud's disqualification **retracted**. **5. The `-027` trace loss is a class, not an incident.** A git operation during a paid run destroyed $0.1547 of evidence. The mitigation is a mirror and a dirty-tree rule — but `-035` (which enforces it) is also unexecuted, and now the executor has git auth, which makes repetition *easier*.

| # | Requirement | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The fold sees an empty seat** (`-033`) | **Not landed, three batches running.** Without it, 12.7% of criteria are unjudged and recorded as agreed |

Items 1–3 are **free** and already queued. Item 4 needs the `-023` re-run with corrected caps. Item 5 is the actual "usable" gate and nothing has been spent on it.

## Verdict

**The engineering is in the top few percent of what I've seen. The product is unshipped.** Eleven days produced a genuinely rigorous, well-instrumented harness with 970 green tests and a measured ledger — and **no one has ever used it, and the last live run did not terminate.**

The bottleneck has moved. It is no longer *"is the harness correct?"* — the answer is mostly yes, and where it isn't, you now know precisely where and why. It is **"does anyone want this, and can they get it running?"** Four of the last twenty PRs touched product behaviour. That is the number to watch.

**The one thing I'd do next is not a new command.** `-033` is written, free, and unlanded — and it is the difference between a system that reports what it measured and one that reports silence as agreement. **Land it, land `-042` and `-046`, then spend the `-023` re-run, then stop measuring and make a stranger able to run it.**

# The decision: **P1 refuted.** The typed layer does not ship.

I predicted the bar would be missed narrowly — $x \in [20,25]$, rate $78.4\%$–$80.9\%$ — and that `-045` would run. Actual: **$x = 35$, rate $86.1\%$.** Not a narrow miss; a comfortable pass, nine criteria to spare.

**I was wrong, and I was wrong in the direction that would have cost you money.** Had my prediction been the basis for the decision, you would have added a managed dependency to fill a seat the validator was already filling. The measurement overruled the architect. That is the strongest possible argument for the pre-registration discipline, and it is the second time this session my prediction has been refuted.

## What I got wrong

My reasoning was: *"if those evidence items clearly addressed their criteria, the prior pass would have classified them addressed."* That assumed the `-038` classifier was calibrated. It wasn't — **its `glossed` bucket was conservative.** It under-assigned to `addressed`, which means `-038`'s headline $68.0\%$ under-reported coverage. The true figure was $86.1\%$ all along.

Note the direction: `-038`'s error **under-claimed** the validator's coverage. That made the case for a new layer look stronger than it was. Convention 26 is usually violated by over-claiming; this is the mirror, and it is just as consequential when the number decides a ruling.

**Consequence, recorded cleanly:** D12's build condition is not met. `ARCH-20260923-045` does not run. The typed judgment layer is **not required** — it remains available as a future option, not a planned one.

## What this result does *not* say — and it is not a rescue attempt

The command explicitly measured **coverage of address, not correctness.** $86.1\%$ means the validator *talks about* $86.1\%$ of abstained criteria. It does not say its verdicts on them are right. That limitation was baked into the instrument by design, so it is a limitation, not a flaw — and I name it as **the next open question**, not as a reason to distrust the result or revisit my prediction.

## The residual, corrected

$$\text{not addressed or attributable} = \frac{3 + 24}{194} = \frac{27}{194} = 13.9\%$$

$$\text{unjudged per criterion} = 0.398 \times 0.139 = 5.5\%$$

$$P(\text{a run carries} \geq 1) = 1 - (1 - 0.055)^{5.81} \approx \mathbf{28\%}$$

Down from my earlier $55\%$ estimate. **And that $28\%$ is still recorded by the fold as agreement, because `-043` has not landed.**

<details open>
<summary><strong>The thing that actually matters here</strong></summary>

Look at what the 27 consists of. Three are **named but not judged**. Twenty-four are **unattributable** — the validator's evidence cannot be paired to a criterion.

For those 24, the validator may well have considered them. **But the fold cannot record a vote it cannot attribute.** So from the fold's perspective, those seats are empty regardless of how good the validator is.

**$86.1\%$ tells us the validator does the work. It does not tell us the fold can see it.** `-043` is what converts an invisible 13.9% into a recorded empty seat — which makes it more important now, not less. It remains the single most important unlanded command, deferred across four batches.

</details>

## 3. Two findings the summary didn't mention

**a) `main`'s HEAD stamp is stale right now, and only PR #66 fixes it.** `HANDOVER.md` on `main` reads `HEAD: c30df9d`, `Tests: 970`, `Date: 2026-09-22` — while `main` is `d952e59` (2026-09-23). `-025` was reported *"re-applied as part of `-043`"*, so the restamp lives **on the branch, not on main.** **Merging PR #66 is what closes B22.** Verify the stamp after merge; if it still reads `c30df9d`, B22 is not closed and `-025` has now failed four times.

**b) My sanity-check arithmetic used a stale figure, and `-042` corrects it.** I wrote $1-0.987^6=7.6\%$ — that used the **pre-abstention** 98.7% presence rate. The true distribution is:

$$\text{presence } 61.3\% \quad\cdot\quad \text{form } 38.3\% \quad\cdot\quad \text{prohibition } 0.3\%$$

**This makes the system sounder than I described, not weaker.** The 38.3% *form* class — the largest non-presence class — **abstains and therefore cannot kill a run.** The 61.3% presence class carries a 1.0% false-fail rate. Recomputing the loop-death risk from a false fail:

$$P(\text{false fail per run}) = 1 - (1-0.01)^{5.81 \times 0.613} \approx 3.5\%$$

**Down from the 7.6% I published.** The residual unjudged surface is $0.383 \times 0.139 = 5.3\%$ of all criteria, giving $\approx 27\%$ of runs carrying at least one — and that is now **recorded as an empty seat rather than as agreement**, which is exactly what `-043` bought.

# Prediction HELD — and it changes what we know

I pre-registered: *case (c) reaches `escalated` and terminates within bounds; if it reaches the ceiling instead, B18 fixed the reporting and not the cause.* **Result: HELD.** 8 implement calls, 31 total AI calls, typed terminal naming the bound, no ceiling. **B18 fixed the cause.**

## What the three cases actually prove, at the code level

**Finding 1 — the loop is bounded on the failure path, and it wasn't before.** The old death was $42$ calls. Case (c) is $31$. The mechanism is now legible: a genuine fail exhausts `build_loop` (5) then `recovery_loop` (3) and **the iteration bounds bite before the call ceiling**. That is the difference between a run that dies and a run that escalates.

$$8 \text{ implement calls} \times \approx 3.9 \text{ calls/iter} \approx 31 \text{ calls} < 41 \text{ ceiling}$$

There's margin. But note it's *not* a proof that the ceiling can never be reached first — a heavier workflow (research tier, review tier) spends more per iteration. Worth keeping in mind, not worth a command today.

**Finding 2 — recovery's bound is its own.** `escalation_recovery_attempts` is separate from `build_loop.max_iterations`, answering my question. The original 42-call death was **not** caused by inheritance. So the fix that mattered was `-034`: coverage no longer false-fails, so the loop stops retrying a criterion it can never satisfy. **In the genuine-fail case the bounds escalate; in the false-fail case there's nothing to fix, so it should have passed or abstained — and now it does.**

**Finding 3 — the fold's empty seat is live and honest.** `abstained_judges={'coverage': 1}`, detail reads *"empty seat, not unanimous"* and **not** *"all judges agree."* `-043` works on a real graph run.

## The gap that case (c) exposes

Look at the terminal verbatim:

> `'recovery_loop' did not converge within 3 iterations, still red: build`

That says **where** it stopped and **which loop** stayed red. It does **not** say **what was never satisfied.** For a genuinely unmet criterion, the operator-critical fact is *which criterion could not be met, after eight attempts, and what was tried* — and the terminal gives the bound, not the diagnosis.

That is convention 28 on the output surface: **the instrument asserts a conclusion ("still red: build") without asserting its subject ("criterion 3: numeric consistency, red in all 8 iterations").** The harness picks the bound but not the reason. For a "working harness," that's the difference between *"it stopped"* and *"here is what it couldn't do."*

**This is the next item, and it's free.**

# Prediction HELD — and the finding is sharper than the fix

I pre-registered: *assertion 1 fails — the terminal names the bound but not the persistent criterion.* **Result: HELD.** Assertion 2 also failed; assertion 3 held. Two of three.

## The code-level reading

The information exists. It is **one to three hops away**, and that is the whole defect:

| Fact | Where it lives | Hops to terminal |
|---|---|---|
| Which criteria stayed unmet | `coverage.missed` | **3** (reason → `judges.dissenting` → `coverage.missed`) |
| What the escalation concluded | `escalation.root_cause_analysis` | **1** |
| A human is needed | `requires_human` | 0 — working |

**This is convention 28 on the output surface, exactly.** The terminal asserts a conclusion — *"still red: build"* — without asserting its subject. A reader cannot tell from the terminal whether one criterion failed or six, or which. **`requires_human` works because it is a field, not a sentence** — and that is the tell: the harness already knows how to carry a machine-readable conclusion, it just doesn't carry the *reason* beside it.

## Ruling — instrument repair, with one condition

The executor asked whether this is a ruling. **It is instrument repair, not a behaviour change** — it alters what the *record carries*, not what any verdict, gate, or model concludes. `_dissent_suffix()` is the existing precedent and it does precisely this.

**But the two facts are not the same kind of fact, and merging them is the one thing that would make this a defect:**

- `coverage.missed` is **measured** — deterministic, produced by a free check.
- `escalation.root_cause_analysis` is a **model's claim** — *"Implementation does not address caching requirements."*

Appending both into one sentence would let a reader mistake a model's diagnosis for the harness's finding. **Convention 26.** So the suffix must **label provenance**:

```
'recovery_loop' did not converge within 3 iterations, still red: build
 — unmet (measured): [criterion 3: numeric consistency; criterion 5: ...]
 — escalation assessment (model): Implementation does not address caching requirements
```

**And the precondition that decides whether this is repair at all:** `-021` found `ScenarioRun.skipped` was decided by **substring-matching the error message.** If *anything* still parses the terminal reason, appending to it is a behaviour change and this stops. That check comes first.

## 2. The finding the merge exposed — and it's the real news

**Merged-main CI FAILED**, on four jobs:

```
test (3.11):      missing greenlet before test collection
editable-install: missing greenlet during startup import
docker:           missing greenlet during container startup
test (3.12):      cancelled after failure
```

Root cause: **`pyproject.toml` declared `sqlalchemy` without the `[asyncio]` extra, while the runtime imports `sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio`.**

**Read what that means.** 979 source-tree tests passed in a developer venv while **a clean install of the package could not import its own database layer.** The code worked because the venv happened to have `greenlet`; the *package* was broken. That is precisely the fault the `editable-install` and `docker` jobs exist to catch — and they caught it on the first merge that ran them against a fresh environment. Repaired in `5dabcaa` (`sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0.36`), with a guard `tests/test_runtime_dependencies.py` that was red before and green after.

**This is a code defect, not a marketing one.** "Works in my venv" and "works" are different claims, and until this merge the harness only had the first. Recorded as **B26**.

The command said *"Record Ruling D15 verbatim"* — **and never contained the text.** The executor reported `PARTIAL` and the owner directed it not to invent one. **That is exactly correct behaviour.**

Note the shape: `AGENTS.md` says *a command citing a sha, a file path, or a measured figure must carry one verifying it.* I wrote a command citing a ruling's text **without carrying the text.** Same class, self-inflicted. The verbatim text is in `-056` below.

## Order

| # | Command | P | Cost | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **-056** | Supply D15, record B26, close the PARTIAL, second precondition exhibit, resolve B7's fold question | **P0** | $0 | Closes my fourth defect of the session |
| **-053** | **Actionable terminal** — the fix `-052` designed | **P0** | $0 | Next code item; ruled; small |
| **-054** | **Recovery succeeds** | **P0** | $0 | Is recovery a mechanism or a delay? |

**My pre-registered predictions:**
- **-053:** nothing parses the reason string, so the append is safe instrument repair; cases (a) and (b) unchanged. If something *does* parse it, the class changes and I'm wrong.
- **-054:** recovery **succeeds and the run completes** — but I expect the finding to be that **recovery receives the same context as the failed build attempt**, i.e. it's a retry wearing a recovery's name. If that's what the code shows, then `recovery_loop` costs three iterations of real money on every failing run and buys nothing, and the remedy is a ruling.

**One line:** verified — `main` is `d733e63`, the stack landed linearly, 980 tests, 86.1% and the fold are on main — and the merge's real prize was catching a **broken clean install that 979 source-tree tests passed straight through**, which is the difference between "works in my venv" and "works"; supply D15 (my fault, third time), then fix the failure terminal and prove recovery recovers.

## The finding: PUSHED-without-a-PR is the same class as CARRIED-without-execution

`-057` did its job well. It named CARRIED, verified the premise rather than assuming it, recorded the corrected merge table, and answered my `-060` questions in the notebook (§65). It even refused to silently rewrite `-056`'s response, leaving it as the exhibit of a PUSHED write that later merged. **That is careful work.**

But look at the shape of the two gaps side by side:

| Artifact | Left half done | Right half missing | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-053`/`-054` | instruction **carried** to main | never **executed** | looks delivered, isn't done |
| `-057` | work **committed and pushed** | no **PR opened** | looks pushed, isn't mergeable |

**Both leave the artifact in a state that reads as progress and is not actionable.** The instruction without execution; the execution without a merge path. That is one defect, and it is D15's own class extended — *an artifact moved, and the step that would make it count did not.*

And it has a cost I can name: **`-057` carries the stamp fix.** `main`'s `HANDOVER.md` still reads `HEAD: 5dabcaa` while `main` is `11be081e` — the B22 stiffness recurring — and the correction is sitting on an unmergeable branch.

**Also worth noting:** `-057` allocated the sqlalchemy fault to **B1's row**, not a new id, and used **B26** for the 12.7% unjudged residual. My `-056` constraint said "use the next available identifier and say which you used" — that satisfies it. The clean-install distinction (979 source-tree tests passed while the package was broken) is recorded in §64.

## Rulings

> **D16 — PUSHED requires a merge path.** A branch with committed work and no PR is not PUSHED; it is **STRANDED**, and it must be named as such in the response. Rationale: D15 says the state of record changes only at merge, so any state from which no merge can occur is not a state the channel can reason about. `delivery_state` must therefore carry the **PR number** where one exists, and a response claiming PUSHED with no PR is a `BLOCKED`-class report, not a DONE. First exhibit: `-057` at `a6dcf6ab`, pushed 05:18:47Z, no PR.

> **D17 — carriage may carry an instruction; it may not carry work.** Answering `-057`'s open question: carriage is legitimate as **transport** — an instruction is a message, and moving it to main without executing it is honest as long as the state (`CARRIED`) is named, which it now is. **But the permission has a boundary: carriage must never carry an artifact that claims work was done.** `-053`/`-054` are instructions, so `4ab956f8` was correct. A response file claiming DONE is not transport and must travel only with the work it describes, on the same branch, as the protocol already requires. So: carriage-without-execution is permitted and named; carriage-of-a-false-claim is not.

## The real priority has not moved

`-057` is documentation. **`-053` and `-054` are the code**, and they have now been CARRIED through two merges without executing:

- **`-053`** — the failure terminal names *which* criterion could not be met, not just *that* a loop stayed red. Three hops collapsed into the record.
- **`-054`** — recovery has only ever been observed failing. If recovery receives the same context as the failed build attempt, it is a retry wearing a recovery's name and costs three iterations of real money on every failing run.

**Both are free and both are already in the channel.** Per the channel's own rule they are new work and process in `command_id` order — they need executing, not re-issuing.

## 3. Rulings

> **D18 — a stamp must name `main` and an ancestor of `main`, or it is not a stamp.** The `-025` freshness guard checks resolvability and ancestry. `2e75232` on a deleted branch satisfies neither intent: it names a *branch* that cannot be checked out. The guard must assert the named branch **exists** and the named commit is an **ancestor of `main`**. Third exhibit of B22, and the first where the guard could have caught it and did not.

> **D19 — a document labelled "verbatim" is a claim, and claims are guarded.** §3.2's manifest block contradicts B1's row in the same file. Either the block is generated from `pyproject.toml` and guarded, or it stops being labelled verbatim. Convention 24, applied to the one section that most invites hand-copying.

# AutoRnD-OS — Qwen / Agent Rules

Multi-model agentic harness for engineering R&D.
Stack: Python 3.11+ / FastAPI / Pydantic v2 / Async SQLAlchemy 2 + aiosqlite / ChromaDB / OpenRouter.

> `AGENTS.md` is the sole protocol authority. Read it before altering harness behavior.

---

## 1. Roles & Permission Boundary

- **Owner:** Holds money, `.env`, serving pins, and standing config.
- **Advisor:** Designs and rules.
- **Executor:** Measures and implements. Proposes, does not rule.

### Boundary: Repair vs. Behavior Change
- **Instrument Repair (Executor OK):** Crash-proofing, retry/retention logic, making counters accurate, fixing wrong measurements.
- **Needs Ruling (Behavior Change):** Verdict semantics, loop exit conditions, gate routing, prompt text altering judgment.

### G-Gates (Owner Only)
- **G-1:** API keys move only via terminal and `.env`.
- **G-2:** Serving pins are proposed with evidence and ratified by owner.
- **G-3:** Owner edits `.env` and standing config. Paid runs require explicit owner approval.

Work channel: `.orchestration/`

---

## 2. Naming & Core Code Patterns

- **Structure:** `snake_case.py` files. Packages: `graph/`, `engine/`, `knowledge/`, `routing/`, `models/`, `specialists/`, `evals/`, `api/`.
- **Helpers & Classes:** Private helpers use leading `_` (`_natural_key`). Classes `PascalCase`. Pydantic verdicts end in `Verdict` (`TriageVerdict`). Exceptions end in `Error` (`SpecError(ValueError)`).
- **Normalisation:** Keys/domains use `normalise_key()`. Never compare raw model strings directly.
- **Type Annotations:** `from __future__ import annotations` at top of every module. Use built-in generics (`dict[str, int]`, `list[str]`, `X | None`).
- **Async & Data:** Async by default on all I/O. Typed Pydantic verdicts over prose.
- **Logging & API:** Use stdlib `logging` (`logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)`). Never `print()` in library code. API errors use `HTTPException(status, "msg")`; success wraps in `{"data": ...}`.
- **Extensibility:** Use `@check("name")` registry in `graph/checks.py` and `getattr(self, f"_phase_{node.prompt}")`.
- **Documentation:** Constants must carry comments explaining *why* and citing live run measurements.

---

## 3. Build & Test Commands

```bash
.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/ -q          # Full suite (<1 min, no network)
.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/test_graph.py -q # Single test file
pip install -e ".[dev]"                         # Install dependencies
uvicorn autornd.main:app --port 8100            # Run local API                         does this match are qwen/md file that we create what would you change or add

| **`AGENTS.md` is the sole protocol** — and it says so in the first paragraph | *"This file is the protocol. There is exactly one copy of it (convention 24)."* |

## 2. What's genuinely good

The boundary split (instrument repair vs. behaviour change), the G-gates, the naming/typing/structure section, and the build commands are all accurate and useful. §2's *"constants must carry comments explaining why and citing live run measurements"* is convention 1 stated plainly. If this were the **only** file, it'd be a solid onboarding doc.

## 3. What's missing, ranked by whether it has already caused a defect

<details open>
<summary><strong>The omissions that would let a new agent repeat a mistake this repo already paid for</strong></summary>

**Tier 1 — caused a real defect, absent from the file:**

| Missing | Why it's dangerous | What it cost |

| **Never parse English for control flow** | Convention 3 is in the file only as "typed verdicts over prose" — the *prohibition* is absent | `-021`: `ScenarioRun.skipped` decided by substring-matching an error message |

| **The meter epoch** — cost predating `b4cd89f` is understated **2.6×–295×** | A new agent citing a cost figure will be wrong by orders of magnitude | AGENTS.md flags it with ⚠️; the file omits it |

**Tier 2 — the operational rules with no home in the file:**

**Non-negotiables 1–7** (free checks before paid calls; measurement comments sacred; no `eval`; enums are default vocabularies; no hardcoded model names — enforced by `tests/test_docs.py`). **Conventions 17–28**, all absent — especially 22 (a test simulates the condition end to end), 24 (generated or guarded, never hand-stamped), 26 (report states what it measured), and 28 (assert you computed your subject first). **Isolate the knowledge store** (`_isolated_store()`). **Private corpora never enter the repo.** **Pin servings before believing a live reading.** **Departures go in §n.2.** **Counts are re-derived, never trusted.**

**Tier 3 — the channel mechanics, reduced to "Work channel: `.orchestration/`":**

`AGENTS.md` documents: `parent_id` must have a response file or it's `BLOCKED`; every command must carry a non-empty `preconditions` array; a precondition failure is `BLOCKED`, *not* a deviation; the `IN_PROGRESS`-commit-before-work rule **and the HEAD-guard collision ruling**; the required response fields; the seven-status vocabulary including `NO_ACTION`; the **always-in-scope set** from `COMMAND_TEMPLATE.json`; and `tests/test_command_template.py`. A new executor reading this file alone would not know it may act as transport, or that it must not modify `commands/`.

## 4. What's stale or wrong

1. **It contradicts itself.** §1 says *"AGENTS.md is the sole protocol authority"* — then restates protocol as rules. If they ever diverge, which wins is unstated. (`AGENTS.md` answers that for `CLAUDE.md`: *"this file wins."* The new file doesn't say it.)
2. **§3 omits the jobs that caught this week's real bug.** `editable-install` and `docker` are the only two that could see the `sqlalchemy[asyncio]` break — **979 source-tree tests passed while a clean install could not import the database layer.** The file lists `pytest` and `pip install -e ".[dev]"` and neither job. It also lacks *run before and after* and *CI green before finishing*.
3. **The stack line states the truth and not the lesson.** "Async SQLAlchemy 2" is correct; the rule that follows from B1 is *the declared dependency contract must match the runtime imports*, guarded by `tests/test_runtime_dependencies.py`.
4. **No reading order.** `AGENTS.md` opens with it: read this → `HANDOVER.md` → last two sections of `docs/handover-review.md`; and `docs/successor-prompt.md` opens a session. The file has no orientation path at all — so a new agent has no way to find the state of record.

## 5. The recommended shape

**Do not add a fourth protocol-shaped document.** Today: `AGENTS.md` (authoritative) + `CLAUDE.md` (declared-derived) + `CONTRIBUTING.md`. A `QWEN.md` restating rules makes **three** rule documents to drift, and the guard scans by content.

Two acceptable shapes, and I'd take the second:

- **(a) Symlink** `QWEN.md` → `AGENTS.md`. Simplest, one source. But the repo moved *away* from this for `CLAUDE.md` — because it replaced a symlink with a content guard *"which is a stronger guard than the symlink it replaced."*

**If the tooling requires the rules inline, generate the file and guard it** — a test asserting its protocol section is identical to `AGENTS.md`'s, the way the repo guards every other derived fact.

````markdown
# QWEN.md — agent working rules

**`AGENTS.md` is the protocol, and it wins.** This file is not a second copy of it.
It carries only what an agent needs in hand to work in this repo — the reading order,
the commands that must pass, the git invariants, and a pointer table of traps that have
already cost this project time. Every rule lives in `AGENTS.md`; this file points at it
rather than restating it.

**Where this file and `AGENTS.md` differ, `AGENTS.md` wins and this file is wrong.**
If you find a conflict, fix this file — do not act on it.

This file is *derived*. It must be guarded by a test that fails if its protocol
section diverges from `AGENTS.md`, in the same way `tests/test_protocol_file.py`
guards against a second copy of the protocol appearing anywhere in the tree.

---

## 1. Opening a session

Read, in order:

1. **`AGENTS.md`** — the protocol. Roles, permission boundary, non-negotiables, conventions, the channel.
2. **`HANDOVER.md`** — the state of record. §2 architecture · §4.2 the bug ledger · §4.4 conventions · §5 the frontier · §6 measured facts.
3. **The last two sections of `docs/handover-review.md`** — the most recent work, pasted before execution with its record.

Then:

4. Run the suite and **report the count**. Do not trust a count written in a document.
5. Report the frontier: open defects in §4.2, and any `.orchestration/commands/<id>.json`
   with no matching `responses/<id>.response.json`.
6. **Stop and wait for the owner.** Change nothing until confirmed.

`docs/successor-prompt.md` is what the owner pastes to open a session.

The shape of the record: `HANDOVER.md` is the state, `docs/handover-review.md` is the
evidence. A claim in the first should be traceable to a run in the second.

---

## 2. Commands that must pass

```bash
.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/ -q          # full suite, free, no network
.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/test_graph.py -q
pip install -e ".[dev]"
uvicorn autornd.main:app --port 8100
```

**Run the suite before and after every change, and report the count both times.**
**CI must be green before you finish.** CI is not the suite — it is three job groups:

- `test` on Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13
- `editable-install` — installs the package clean and imports it
- `docker` — builds the image, starts it, hits `/api/health`

**`editable-install` and `docker` are not redundant.** A change once passed the whole
source-tree suite while a clean install could not import its own database layer: the
declared manifest omitted a dependency extra that the runtime imported. Only those two
jobs could see it. If you touch `pyproject.toml` or add an import, watch them.

---

## 3. Git — what you may do, and the invariants

You create branches, commit, push, and open pull requests. You commit command files
verbatim as carriage.

**Merges to `main` are the owner's** unless the owner grants merge-on-green in one line.

Invariants — no exceptions, no approvals:

- **No force-push. No history rewrite. No deletion on a protected branch.**
- **No direct push to `main`.**
- **No git operation while a paid run is in flight.** This destroyed a run's entire
  trace once: the writer kept the inode, the stash took the directory entry, and every
  unit record went to a deleted file.
- **A paid run must not start on a dirty working tree.**
- **Never move a key through chat, in either direction.** Keys move only via the
  terminal and `.env`.

---

## 4. Channel delivery states

A response saying `DONE` means **the work is pushed**, not that it is on `main`.
Name the state you are in:

| State | Means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **MERGED** | ancestor of `main`. The only state that changes the record | nothing |
| **PUSHED** | committed on a branch, **PR open** | record the PR number |
| **STRANDED** | commits on a branch, **no PR** | open the PR — this is not a delivery |
| **CARRIED** | command file on `main`, no response file | still new work; execute in `command_id` order |

A branch with commits and no pull request is not pushed. A command file being an
ancestor of `HEAD` proves it was *delivered*, not that it was *done*.

---

## 5. Traps — pointer table

Each of these has already cost this project time. One line of consequence; follow the
pointer for the rule.

| Trap | What it cost | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Parsing English for control flow | A run's status was decided by substring-matching an error message; correcting the message broke it inside the same change | Non-negotiable 3, `AGENTS.md` §4.4 |
| A paid call before a free check | — | Non-negotiable 2: free checks preempt paid calls |
| A test double that doesn't bill | A free double hid a real accounting bug | Convention 7 (`client._account`) |
| An unisolated knowledge store | Every gap came back pre-answered from a local Chroma directory | `_isolated_store()` |
| Citing a cost figure from before the meter epoch | Figures understated by 2.6×–295× | `AGENTS.md` ⚠️ Meter epoch |
| A paid run without a committed pre-registration | The commit is the only evidence the prediction preceded the result | Working rules; a wrong prediction is reported as wrong |
| An instrument tested on a mock return | Five instruments reported less than they measured, every one against a green suite | Convention 22: simulate the condition end to end |
| A count or fact written by hand | Twelve drifts in one document | Convention 24: generated or guarded, never hand-stamped |
| A report that reads as more than it measured | Four exhibits in one week | Convention 26 |
| An instrument asserting a conclusion without asserting its subject | An empty match set reported as no problem | Convention 28 |
| A command citing evidence nobody checked | A command cited an entire paid run — calls, dollars, traces, two shas — none of which existed | Orchestration: run every precondition first |
| Trusting `--max-spend` to cap a sweep | `--repeat 2` under a $0.50 sweep cap could only ever start one unit | `--max-spend` caps one scenario-run; `--max-spend-sweep` caps the sweep |

---

## 6. Rule index

Where each class of rule lives. Do not copy the rule here.

| Class | Location |
|---|---|
| Roles, permission boundary, G-gates | `AGENTS.md` §Who decides what |
| Non-negotiables 1–7 | `AGENTS.md` §Non-negotiables, `HANDOVER.md` §4.4 |
| Conventions 17–28 | `HANDOVER.md` §4.4 (full text and the measurement behind each) |
| The command channel | `AGENTS.md` §Orchestration, `.orchestration/README.md`, `COMMAND_TEMPLATE.json` |
| The bug ledger and the frontier | `HANDOVER.md` §4.2, §5 |
| Measured facts and their provenance | `HANDOVER.md` §6 |
| Architecture and the node kinds | `HANDOVER.md` §2 |

**Permission boundary in one line:** you measure and implement; you do not rule. A change
to what the harness *concludes* — verdict semantics, loop exit conditions, gate routing,
prompt text that steers judgment — needs a ruling. Where a blueprint is silent and the
answer changes a conclusion, record the question and ask. The full boundary is in
`AGENTS.md` and it is the one that counts.

---

## 7. Maintaining this file

- **A rule belongs in `AGENTS.md`.** If you find yourself wanting to add a rule here,
  add it there instead and point at it.
- **No counts.** No test totals, no sha stamps, no dates. A count here is a hand-stamp
  that will drift, and the repo has the scars.
- **No model ids.** `tests/test_docs.py` enforces this.
- **Keep it short enough to read in one sitting.** Its job is orientation, not authority.
````
